status: SKELETON — empty plumbing. No RWE records yet (corpus.realWorldExamples == []). Data populated downstream, lighter than the flagship.

parent_family.relation: Sibling vendoring of the flagship RWE family for anchor + export-discipline compatibility, sized down for a small library. Heavier attestation fields (short_quote_attestation_status / verbatim_recovery_status / archetype_signal_* / frame_inversion / layer_skepticism / public_reach / refutation_variant_id) are INHERITABLE FROM THE PARENT per record when needed — NOT required at launch.

anchor_discipline: instance_id values are APPEND-ONLY deep-link anchors (recommended rwe-<id> family) — never recycled, mirroring the objection #obj-<id> covenant.
binding: RWE records live in corpus.realWorldExamples[]. Each attaches to >=1 objection via attached_objections[].objection_id (foreign key into corpus.objections[].id). Objection nodes carry rwe_refs[] as the reverse slot (an array of instance_id).

example_record_schema._doc: Core/lighter record fields. Sized-down subset of the flagship example_record_schema; extend from the parent as a record needs it. Enum value-sets marked values_ref inherit the parent's canonical lists rather than restating (and risking drift from) them.

archive_url._doc: corpus-decay hedge; recommended for fragile sources

validation_rules._doc: Core rules vendored from the parent for anchor + export discipline. The rwe_refs-resolve check is implemented in right_to_die_validator_v0_1.py (check_rwe) and is VACUOUS while realWorldExamples == [] — it engages automatically when RWE data lands.
rules: v4_foreign_key_validity — attached_objections[].objection_id resolves to corpus objections[].id
rwe_refs_resolve — every objection.rwe_refs[] resolves to a realWorldExamples[].instance_id (both directions)
